title: Where Do Vision Language Models Fail at 3D Reasoning?
abstract: arXiv:2610.39639v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Vision-language models can get individual judgments right while struggling to recover and consistently use the exact properties of a 3D object. To characterize this gap, we introduce BedBench, a controlled benchmark of thirteen procedurally generated tasks spanning individual judgments and composite answers. Across twelve open-weight and four frontier models, per-color counting exposes a pronounced weakness: humans achieve 93.3% accuracy, compared with 7.2% for the best model. Targeted fine-tuning raises one model's accuracy from 3.0% to 68.6%, but reveals a further difficulty: its answers about the most common colors remain inconsistent with its own per-color counts. Supplying those counts as text improves its judgments, showing that recovering a property does not mean using it consistently. translated_title: 视觉语言模型在3D推理中会在哪里失败？
translated_abstract: 视觉语言模型能够做出正确的单独判断，却难以恢复并一致地使用3D对象的精确属性。为了刻画这一差距，我们推出了BedBench，这是一个包含十三个程序化生成任务的受控基准，涵盖单独判断和复合回答。在十二个开源权重模型和四个前沿模型的评估中，按颜色计数任务暴露出一个明显的弱点：人类达到93.3%的准确率，而表现最好的模型仅为7.2%。针对性的微调将一个模型的准确率从3.0%提升至68.6%，但揭示出进一步的困难：该模型关于最常见颜色的回答仍然与其自身的按颜色计数结果不一致。将这些计数以文本形式提供给模型可以改善其判断，这表明恢复某个属性并不意味着能够一致地使用它。推理、规模扩展和增加视觉线索各自都能改善单独判断，但没有一项能让精确回答变得可靠。为了定位这一困难的根源，我们……
tldr: 该论文提出BedBench基准，揭示视觉语言模型在3D推理中虽然能做出正确的单独判断，却难以恢复并一致使用3D物体的精确属性（如按颜色计数任务中最佳模型仅达7.2%准确率），且即使通过微调和提供文本计数信息能改善表现，模型依然无法可靠地给出精确答案。
en_tdlr: The paper introduces BedBench, a controlled benchmark revealing that vision-language models, despite making correct individual judgments in 3D reasoning, struggle to recover and consistently use exact object properties—where even targeted fine-tuning, reasoning, scaling, and textual count information fail to make exact answers reliable.
